mainTopic: Engagement gifts that must be returned, and how a שכיב מרע's gift depends on what he really intended (אומדנא)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a man who went into a ruin to test his ארוסה's sense of smell. The ruin fell and she died, and the חכמים rule that he does not inherit from her. Next, the גמרא returns to the engagement gifts (סבלונות) from the משנה. רבין סבא explains that the gifts go back if someone died or he backed out, and that if she backed out even food goes back. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע adds that meat is paid back at up to a third off. A new משנה rules that a שכיב מרע who gave away all his property, and kept no land, can cancel the gift if he recovers. The גמרא asks which תנא follows this reading of a person's unspoken intent (אומדנא). רב נחמן says it is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, and רב ששת says it is רבי שמעון שזורי. Each one explains why the other's source is different. The amud ends by starting a new question about a bedridden man asked who should get his property, and his answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the story: the woman dies in the ruin and he does not inherit
steps.stepSummary: The story ends. She shows she can smell the dates, the ruin collapses and she dies, and the חכמים rule that he does not inherit from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: 'Who will give us some Jericho dates to eat?' The ruin fell on her and she died. The חכמים said: since he only went in after her to test her, and not to marry her, he does not inherit from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story it started earlier and gives the חכמים's ruling at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He went into the ruin only to check her sense of smell, so it does not count as completing the marriage (נישואין). She was still only his ארוסה when she died. That is why he does not inherit from her.
steps.whatToRemember: Going in with a woman just to test her does not complete the marriage, so a husband who only did ארוסין does not inherit.

phrases.english: She said to him: Who will give us
some of the dates of Jericho, so I can eat them?
phrases.notes: She was hinting that she smelled the date he brought in. So her sense of smell works fine.

phrases.english: The ruin fell on her, and she died.
The Sages said: Since he did not go in
after her except to test her,
if she dies, he does not inherit from her.
phrases.notes: She was only engaged to him (ארוסה), and a man does not inherit from a woman he is only engaged to.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: הוֹאִיל וְלֹא נִכְנַס אַחֲרֶיהָ אֶלָּא לְבוֹדְקָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Entering with her only to test her is not נישואין, so he does not inherit his ארוסה.

steps.title: רבין סבא explains when engagement gifts go back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about small engagement gifts. Then רבין סבא rules: if either one dies or the man backs out, the gifts go back but food does not. If she backs out, everything goes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A few gifts for her to use in her father's house, etc.' רבין סבא sat before רב פפא and said: Whether she died, he died, or he backed out, the gifts go back but food and drink do not. If she backed out, even a bundle of vegetables goes back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about סבלונות, and רבין סבא gives a rule for when these gifts must be returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין's rule depends on who ended the engagement. If he backed out, or someone died, she returns the lasting gifts but keeps whatever was eaten. If she backed out, she must return everything, even something as small as vegetables.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts a man sends his bride during the engagement

steps.confusionAlert: The word הדר is used in two senses here: 'he backed out' and 'it goes back' (is returned). Read each one carefully.

phrases.english: A few engagement gifts
for her to use in her father's house, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, which said these small gifts are not collected back.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רָבִין סָבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: Ravin the Elder was sitting before Rav Pappa,
and he sat and said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁמֵּתָה הִיא וּבֵין שֶׁמֵּת הוּא,
phrases.english: Whether she died or whether he died,
or he backed out, the gifts go back,
but food and drink do not go back.
If she backed out,
even a bundle of vegetables goes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רָבִין סָבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא, וְיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's topic of engagement gifts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If either one died or he backed out, the gifts go back but food and drink do not. If she backed out, everything goes back, even a bundle of vegetables.

steps.title: Meat is paid back at a lowered price
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע adds that when payment is made for meat, the court values it at a cheaper price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: And we value the meat for them at a cheap price.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a detail to the rule about returning gifts: how to put a price on meat that must be paid for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat was already eaten, so the family pays its value instead of handing it back. That value is set lower than what the man paid, so the woman's family is not charged full price.

keyTerms.meaning: We assess or appraise the value

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
And we assess for them the value of meat at a cheap price.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְשָׁמִין לָהֶן דְּמֵי בָשָׂר בְּזוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how repayment for food is calculated
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat that is paid for is valued at a reduced price.

steps.title: How much cheaper?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how big the discount is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact size of the discount רב הונא mentioned. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'cheap' is vague. The גמרא wants a clear number that a court can actually use.

phrases.english: Up to how much is "cheap"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the size of the discount
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact size of the discount on the meat

steps.title: Up to one-third less
steps.stepSummary: The discount is up to one-third.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the meat is valued at up to one-third less than its price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives the vague word 'cheap' a fixed limit. The discount can go as far as one-third off.
steps.whatToRemember: Gifts go back depending on who ended the engagement, and eaten meat is paid back at up to a third off.

phrases.english: Up to one-third.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The discount is up to one-third.

steps.title: New משנה: a dying man who gives away all his property
steps.stepSummary: If a שכיב מרע gives away everything but keeps some land, the gift stands. If he keeps nothing, the gift does not stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person on his deathbed who wrote all his property over to others: if he kept any amount of land for himself, his gift stands. If he did not keep any land at all, his gift does not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a gift given by a person who thinks he is dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he gave away everything, we assume he did it only because he expected to die. So if he recovers, the gift is cancelled. If he kept some land, that shows he meant the gift to stand even if he lives.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is very sick and expects to die
He kept some back for himself
Any amount of land, even a little

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source for the idea that a שכיב מרע's gift depends on what he really had in mind.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person on his deathbed
who wrote all his property over to others,
and he kept any amount of land for himself,
his gift stands.
If he did not keep any amount of land,
his gift does not stand.
phrases.notes: This means if he gets better. He clearly did not plan to leave himself with nothing to live on.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתַב כׇּל נְכָסָיו לַאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping some land makes the gift final. Giving away everything makes it depend on his dying.

steps.title: Which תנא follows 'reading his intent'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows, since it relies on guessing the giver's unspoken intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that we go by an assessment of a person's intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows. This sets up רב נחמן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man never said 'this gift is only if I die.' The משנה cancels the gift based on what he obviously meant. The גמרא wants to know which תנא accepts this kind of reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: An assessment of what a person clearly intended, even if he never said it

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who is the tanna
who holds that we follow an assessment of intent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source opinion behind the משנה

steps.title: רב נחמן: It is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן names רבי שמעון בן מנסיא as the תנא behind the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question by naming the תנא. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming the תנא means the משנה follows one side of a known dispute. The proof that this תנא relies on אומדנא comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who goes by a person's obvious intent

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
It is the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.title: Proof: the father who wrongly heard his son had died
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a father gave everything away after hearing his son had died, and then the son came back. The תנא קמא says the gift stands. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא cancels it because the father would never have given it had he known.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A man's son went overseas, and he heard that his son died. He then wrote all his property to someone else, and afterward his son came back. His gift is valid. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: his gift is not valid, because if he had known his son was alive, he would not have written it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי שמעון בן מנסיא goes by a person's obvious intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father never stated a condition, but it is obvious he gave everything away only because he thought his son was dead. The תנא קמא ignores this unspoken intent, while רבי שמעון בן מנסיא cancels the gift because of it. That is the same reasoning our משנה uses.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
Had it not been that, if only

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה cancels a שכיב מרע's gift based on his obvious intent, which matches רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's view of אומדנא.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָלַךְ בְּנוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.english: As it is taught: In a case where one's son went overseas,
and he heard that his son died,
and he went and wrote all his property over to another person,
and afterward his son came back,
his gift is a valid gift.
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
His gift is not a valid gift,
because had he known that his son was alive,
he would not have written them over.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָלַךְ בְּנוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון בן מנסיא follows אומדנא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the father whose son was wrongly reported dead

steps.title: רב ששת names a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the משנה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is the opinion of רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a second answer to the question of whose opinion the משנה follows. He sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן named רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. רב ששת names a different תנא, רבי שמעון שזורי, who also follows a person's unspoken intent. The proof for his choice comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who rules that we follow a dangerously ill man's likely intent
'It is', meaning the משנה follows this opinion

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is the opinion of Rabbi Shimon Shezuri

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 7, as an alternative to רב נחמן's answer in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.

steps.title: The case of 'write a גט for my wife'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a man who says only 'write a גט' in a moment of danger has it written and given. רבי שמעון שזורי adds that this applies even to a dangerously ill man.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: At first they used to say: A man being led out in a collar to be executed who said 'Write a גט for my wife' — they should write it and give it. Later they said: The same applies to one setting sail or leaving with a caravan. רבי שמעון שזורי says: It applies even to one who is dangerously ill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that supports רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man only said 'write,' but we assume he also meant 'give,' because of his dangerous situation. רבי שמעון שזורי applies this guess even to a sick person. That matches our משנה, where we assume the dying man gave everything away only because he expected to die.

keyTerms.meaning: A collar or chain placed on someone being led to execution
One who sets sail on a sea voyage
A caravan traveling to a far-off place

phrases.english: As it is taught: At first they used to say:
One who goes out in a collar, and said:
phrases.notes: He is being taken out to be executed.

phrases.english: 'Write a get for my wife'
these people should write it and give it.
phrases.notes: He never said 'give,' but we assume that is what he wanted.

phrases.english: They later said:
Even one who sets sail and one who leaves with a caravan.
Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even one who is dangerously ill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב ששת's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה matches a תנא who follows a sick person's unspoken intent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about 'write a גט', where רבי שמעון שזורי includes a dangerously ill man.

steps.title: Why רב נחמן rejects רבי שמעון שזורי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן did not attribute the משנה to רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן, what is the reason he does not explain the משנה according to רבי שמעון שזורי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן did not use רב ששת's source. It sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון שזורי also seems to follow a sick person's unspoken intent. So it is fair to ask why רב נחמן chose a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it up or explains it (as following a certain opinion)

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman, what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא מוֹקֵים לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי?
phrases.english: that he does not explain it according to Rabbi Shimon Shezuri?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מוֹקֵים לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רב ששת's source with רב נחמן's choice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב נחמן did not attribute the משנה to רבי שמעון שזורי.

steps.title: There he at least said 'write'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds that the גט case is different, because the man actually said 'write.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he said 'write.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב נחמן sees a difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גט case, the man spoke and partly showed what he wanted by saying 'write.' In our משנה, the dying man said nothing about why he gave the gift. So guessing his intent is a bigger step, and רבי שמעון שזורי might not go that far.

phrases.english: It is different there, because he said 'write.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the גט case he partly said what he wanted by saying 'write'; in the משנה he said nothing.

steps.title: Why רב ששת rejects רבי שמעון בן מנסיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב ששת did not attribute the משנה to רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת, what is the reason he does not explain the משנה according to רבי שמעון בן מנסיא?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the same question the other way around. It sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא openly cancels a gift based on the giver's unspoken intent. So why did רב ששת not use that clearer source?

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who cancelled the father's gift when the son came back

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet, what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא מוֹקֵים לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא?
phrases.english: that he does not explain it according to Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מוֹקֵים לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 12, now asking about רב ששת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב ששת did not attribute the משנה to רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.title: A clearly proven guess is different
steps.stepSummary: In the father-and-son case, the father's intent is obvious, so it may not teach us about our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A clearly proven assessment is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב ששת did not rely on רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the son came back alive, it was obvious that the father gave everything away only because he thought his son was dead. In our משנה, the dying man's intent is much less obvious. So רבי שמעון בן מנסיא might cancel a gift only when the intent is that clear.

keyTerms.meaning: An assessment or estimate of a person's unspoken intent
That is clearly proven or obvious

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא picks the source that fits best and points to a weakness in the other: רב נחמן says the גט case had a spoken word ('write'), and רב ששת says the father-and-son case had an obvious intent.

phrases.english: A clearly proven assessment is different.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's intent in that ברייתא was obvious; the dying man's intent in the משנה is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that not every guess about a person's intent carries the same weight. An obvious, proven intent is stronger than a weaker guess.

steps.title: Who taught the case of the sick man asked about his property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught a ברייתא about a bedridden man who is asked who should get his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught what the רבנן taught: A man who was sick and lying in bed, and they said to him, 'To whom does your property go?' And he said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about another ברייתא. It starts quoting the case, and the quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a sick man who is asked who should get his property. His answer and the ruling come next. The question 'who taught this' tells us the ruling must be unusual enough to need a named author.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא who taught this?

phrases.english: Who taught that which the Rabbis taught:
One who was sick and lying in bed,
and they said to him: To whom does your property go?
And he said to them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the משנה's source and opens a new question about another ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the author of the ברייתא about the bedridden man asked about his property.
